text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- President Arpad Goncz opened a historic visit to NATO headquarters in Brussels yesterday as the first Hungarian head of state to visit.
- Prime Ministers Gyula Horn and Nicolae Vacaroiu signed the Hungarian-Romanian basic treaty as thousands protested in Timisoara and elsewhere both in Romania and Hungary.
- The Temes county chapter of the Democratic Federation of Hungarians in Romania staged an ecumenical vigil at a Catholic church in Timisoara.

- The economic cabinet expects a 4.5 percent deficit of GDP for 1997. No consumption tax will be levied on chocolate and chewing gum next year, while that of coffee and precius metals will be reduced. Consumption tax rates will rise an average of 14-15 percent.
- An IMF delegation opened a week of negotiations in Budapest yesterday.
- The National Bank of Hungary again lowered its active and passive repo interest rates by 0.25 percent yesterday.

- EBRD is extending a DM7.7 million long-term loan to the printing press Szikra and increasing the firm's capital by another DM4 million to obtain a 19.2 percent stake. Postabank and the publisher Lang Kiado increased their participation to 32.4 percent.
- Local governments will receive stakes in their regional gas distribution companies in the near future.
- Parliament yesterday began debating a bill on home purchase funds.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Finnish Foreign Minister Tarja Halone is to hold talks in Budapest today.

- Slovak Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik said that he wants to discuss an out-of-court settlement to the Gabcikovo dam project, and is ready to discuss minority issues during his upcoming visit to Budapest.
- Penny Market, a subsidiary of the Cologne-based Rewe, Europe's second largest food retailer, will open 250-300 discount food stores throughout Hungary by the end of next year.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Opel Hungary is appealing to the Constitutional Court regarding the Public Procurement Act, following its recent exclusion from a tender to supply vehicles to government offices and ministries.

- The national railway company MAV has sent its development plan and the feasibility study of its planned HUF 100 billion investments to the European Investment Bank, the EBRD and to the PHARE centre.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- The Finnish-Japanese consortium IVO-Tomen has submitted a new bid for the power plant Budapest Eromu after withdrawing its initial offer on hearing that energy price hike will be postponed to next January.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- An international conference will be held at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences in Budapest September 26-29 to mark the upcoming 40th anniversary of the 1956 revolution.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
